title: [CmdPal] Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.exe crashes on startup with System.NotImplementedException in AppLifecycle.GetActivatedEventArgs when running elevated / EnableLUA=0

judgment.rationale: The exception and first call site are explicit in the report, and current main contains the same unguarded call in DecideRedirection plus a second call in OnLaunched. A narrow unsupported-activation fallback is actionable, with launch semantics requiring validation.
evidence: The issue reports System.NotImplementedException/E_NOTIMPL from GetActivatedEventArgs in Program.DecideRedirection under elevated EnableLUA=0 startup.
Current upstream main at 2d28a562bfb5f8a76c4a43bbd8c3939f827bb368 calls GetActivatedEventArgs unguarded in Program.cs::DecideRedirection.
Current upstream main also calls GetActivatedEventArgs unguarded in App.xaml.cs::OnLaunched, so a fix limited to the reported first call would leave another failure path.
The issue gives an exact Windows build, package version, installation method, and startup sequence.
judgment.recommended_action: Add a narrow unsupported-activation fallback at both startup call sites, preserve supported redirection, and validate it in a disposable EnableLUA=0 environment.

fix_assessment.rationale: The failure mechanism is confirmed, but the correct launch context when AppInstance activation arguments are unavailable needs a focused compatibility test.

proposed_fixes.title: Handle unavailable activation arguments during CmdPal startup
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Program.DecideRedirection calls AppInstance.GetCurrent().GetActivatedEventArgs without handling the E_NOTIMPL/NotImplementedException reported for elevated processes with EnableLUA=0. App.OnLaunched repeats the same unguarded call, so a first-call-only catch would not complete startup.
plan: Introduce a narrow, shared activation-argument retrieval path that handles only the unsupported NotImplementedException/E_NOTIMPL case and leaves unrelated failures visible.

When activation arguments are unavailable, skip redirection for that launch and start CmdPal through a safe cold-launch path; update OnLaunched to consume the shared result or normal launch arguments instead of calling the unsupported API again.
Preserve existing activation redirection whenever the API returns arguments, and document which launch data cannot be forwarded in the unsupported case.
Add focused tests for the unsupported activation-argument path and supported single-instance activation forwarding.
verification: In a disposable Windows 11 VM snapshot, run the reported elevated/EnableLUA=0 startup scenario and verify CmdPal reaches its UI without an unhandled exception or modal crash dialog.
Repeat with normal UAC and a second activation to confirm existing single-instance redirection still works.
Run focused CmdPal startup tests covering available and unavailable activation arguments.

confidence.rationale: The reported stack and current source establish the failing call and a second unguarded call, but the safe cold-launch/activation fallback must be validated in the affected environment.

issue_context.summary: Command Palette startup can terminate when AppInstance.GetActivatedEventArgs throws NotImplementedException under an elevated token with EnableLUA=0.
known_information: The reporter gives a repeatable Windows 11 25H2 startup scenario with PowerToys 0.102.3001, CmdPal enabled, elevation, and EnableLUA=0.
The reported Event ID 1026 stack identifies AppInstance.GetActivatedEventArgs called from Program.DecideRedirection as the throwing call.
Current upstream main at 2d28a562bfb5f8a76c4a43bbd8c3939f827bb368 calls GetActivatedEventArgs without a guard in Program.DecideRedirection and calls it again in App.OnLaunched.
inferences: Catching only the first call would leave a second unhandled failure when the application reaches OnLaunched.
When activation arguments are unavailable, startup must avoid redirecting an activation it cannot forward while preserving supported single-instance behavior.
issue_context.analysis: The root exception and first call site are directly supported by the report and current source. Handle the expected unsupported-API path at both call sites and define a safe cold-launch fallback without swallowing unrelated exceptions or regressing supported activation forwarding.
initial_investigation: Read the full issue report and stack trace; no follow-up comments were present in the live snapshot.
Read Program.cs and App.xaml.cs from current upstream main at 2d28a562bfb5f8a76c4a43bbd8c3939f827bb368; both independently call GetActivatedEventArgs without a guard.
No product code was changed and no elevated/EnableLUA=0 reproduction was run.

design.title: Handle unavailable activation arguments during CmdPal startup

reproduce.version_requirement: Reported PowerToys 0.102.3001 / Microsoft.CommandPalette 0.13.13001; candidate build for verification
prerequisites: Use a disposable Windows 11 25H2 VM or snapshot with CmdPal enabled.
Configure the reported elevated startup and EnableLUA=0 only in that disposable test environment.
steps: Reboot or sign in and observe whether Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.exe reaches the UI.
After the fix, repeat the same startup and confirm no unhandled NotImplementedException or crash dialog occurs.
In a normal-UAC run, launch a second activation and confirm it is still forwarded to the existing CmdPal instance.
reproduce.expected_result: CmdPal starts safely when activation arguments are unsupported and retains normal redirection when they are available.

status.label: Startup crash
status.detail: The reported activation API exception is unhandled during CmdPal startup.

next_action.label: Review startup fallback design
